# Introduction 

```{python}
import pandas as pd 
import numpy as np 

import seaborn as sns

sns.set_context('talk')

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = sns.load_dataset('diamonds')
```
The diamonds dataset form seaborn offers a great opportunity to learn more about correlation analysis in Python and Quarto where we will be working with data from `{python} f"{df.shape[0]}"` diamonds and our research question is to study whether the carat of the diamond is correlated with the depth of the diamond.

# Literature Review 


# Method 

Given that we have two columns of continuous data (carat of diomand and depth of diamond), we will evaluate this relationship using simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these.  

# Results

```{python}
corr_val = np.array(df[['carat', 'depth']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > 0.8:
	narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0.4:
	narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
	narrative = "a weak positive correlation" 
elif corr_val > -0.4:
	narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"
```
Using the classic simple Pearson correlation approach these data produce a correlation coefficient of `{python} f"{corr_val:.5f}"`, so we conclude the relationship is `{python} f"{narrative}"`.  

```{python}
#| label: fig-length-width-scatterplot
#| fig-cap: "A scatterplot of diamond carat and depth"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize = (6, 3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data = df, y = 'depth', x = 'carat')

plt.ylabel('Depth')
plt.xlabel('Carat')
```
As shown in @fig-length-width-scatterplot we see additional evidence of a weak positive correlative relationship. 

# Discussion 

Now we know how to do correlation coefficient analysis from this example work-through of the diamond dataset using Python and Quarto and we have found a weak positive correlative relationship.
